correctness.rationale: The Cayley transform and principal square root map the disk conformally onto a convex sector; translation yields a normalized convex univalent f. Differentiating f gives \(A=(t+1)(t^2+1)/(4t)\) and \(P=(3t^4+1)/(4t^2)\). The chosen rational-complex t has \(\operatorname{Re}t>|\operatorname{Im}t|\), so its inverse Cayley z is interior. The exact rational real part of the source-defined component at \(\alpha=1/2\) lies strictly between -1/2 and -1/4, and denominators are nonzero. An independently derived derivative expression and a stand-alone exact Fraction checker verify the identities; no finite enumeration is used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The source specifically identifies this unproved positivity conjecture as the missing hypothesis in a Graham–Kohr extension program. A rigorous negative witness settles that universal assertion, including its pointwise reformulation, using a natural convex-sector mapping. The negative point lies very close to the circle and evades the source’s finite positive Monte Carlo examples. The contribution is a motivated structural counterexample, not a routine small numerical improvement or mere normalization test.
